objects.description: Opaque forward declaration of the JavaScript runtime context used by the Micro QuickJS engine. It is constructed and owned by the API via JS_NewContext/JS_NewContext2 and freed with JS_FreeContext. Internals are not exposed in this header.
Machine word-sized unsigned integer used by the engine for tables and low-level data. Size depends on pointer width (64-bit on JS_PTR64, else 32-bit).

Tagged JavaScript value representation used throughout the API. Encodes integers, pointers, and special values using tag bits. Construct via helpers like JS_NewInt32/JS_NewFloat64/JS_NewString and others. Not a managed struct; lifetime semantics depend on engine GC and rooting helpers (JSGCRef).

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
    JS_CLASS_OBJECT,
    JS_CLASS_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_C_FUNCTION,
    JS_CLASS_CLOSURE,
    JS_CLASS_NUMBER,
    JS_CLASS_BOOLEAN,
    JS_CLASS_STRING,
    JS_CLASS_DATE,
    JS_CLASS_REGEXP,

    JS_CLASS_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_EVAL_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_RANGE_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_REFERENCE_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_SYNTAX_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_TYPE_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_URI_ERROR,
    JS_CLASS_INTERNAL_ERROR,

    JS_CLASS_ARRAY_BUFFER,
    JS_CLASS_TYPED_ARRAY,

    JS_CLASS_UINT8C_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_INT8_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_UINT8_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_INT16_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_UINT16_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_INT32_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_UINT32_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_FLOAT32_ARRAY,
    JS_CLASS_FLOAT64_ARRAY,

    JS_CLASS_USER, /* user classes start from this value */
} JSObjectClassEnum;
objects.description: Enumeration of built-in and user class IDs for JS objects. Used with object creation and error helpers. JS_CLASS_USER marks the starting value for user-defined classes.
Enumeration indexing predefined C functions within the standard library/function tables. JS_CFUNCTION_USER is the first user-reserved slot.
Small temporary buffer used to hold short C strings or scratch space during JS_ToCString/JS_ToCStringLen calls. The exact usage is internal; caller provides storage to avoid allocations.

Node for a GC rooting stack/list used to protect JSValue from garbage collection during C code execution. Use JS_PushGCRef/JS_PopGCRef or JS_AddGCRef/JS_DeleteGCRef; macros JS_PUSH_VALUE/JS_POP_VALUE assist with scoped rooting.

objects.definition: typedef JSValue JSCFunction(JSContext *ctx, JSValue *this_val, int argc, JSValue *argv);
objects.description: Function type for generic C functions callable from JS. Returns a JSValue. Variants with magic/params exist in JSCFunctionType.
Function pointer type for C finalizers associated with opaque data on JS objects. Must not call JS functions from within the finalizer per comment.

objects.definition:
typedef enum JSCFunctionDefEnum {  /* XXX: should rename for namespace isolation */
    JS_CFUNC_generic,
    JS_CFUNC_generic_magic,
    JS_CFUNC_constructor,
    JS_CFUNC_constructor_magic,
    JS_CFUNC_generic_params,
    JS_CFUNC_f_f,
} JSCFunctionDefEnum;
objects.description: Enumeration identifying which variant of C function implementation is used when defining a function (generic, with magic, constructor forms, parameterized, or double->double).
Union of function pointer variants used to store the implementation of a C function exposed to JS, matching the kind specified by JSCFunctionDefEnum.
Definition record for a C function exposed to JS, including the function pointer (variant in func), its name (as JSValue atom/string), definition type, argument count, and optional magic value.

Descriptor of the built-in standard library for Micro QuickJS. Provides pointers to host-provided tables (stdlib_table, C functions, finalizers) and layout/offset metadata. Passed to JS_NewContext/JS_NewContext2.

objects.definition: typedef void JSWriteFunc(void *opaque, const void *buf, size_t buf_len);
objects.description: Writer callback type used for logging/debug output via JS_SetLogFunc. Writes buf_len bytes from buf to an opaque sink.
Interrupt callback type invoked to decide whether JS execution should be interrupted. Return non-zero to request interruption.
Header structure found at the beginning of a relocated bytecode buffer. Holds relocation base address and references to unique strings and the main function as JSValue handles.
32-bit on-disk bytecode header layout used when preparing 32-bit bytecode on a 64-bit host. Only defined when building with JSW==8 guard. Represents 32-bit offsets instead of pointer-sized fields.

functions.name: JS_PushGCRef
functions.description: Pushes a JSGCRef onto the GC root stack and returns a pointer to a JSValue slot associated with it. Typically used to temporarily root a JSValue across operations that may trigger GC. Usage pattern is demonstrated by the JS_PUSH_VALUE macro (push, assign .val, later pop).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext created by JS_NewContext/JS_NewContext2.
ref must point to a valid, writable JSGCRef storage whose lifetime extends until it is popped or deleted.
Push/pop order for this stack-based API should be LIFO (as implied by naming and matching JS_PopGCRef).

functions.name: JS_PopGCRef
functions.description: Pops a previously pushed JSGCRef from the GC root stack and returns the contained JSValue. Intended to pair with JS_PushGCRef to unroot a temporary value. See JS_POP_VALUE macro for typical usage.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
ref must have been previously pushed with JS_PushGCRef and not yet popped.
Calls should match LIFO order of JS_PushGCRef invocations.

functions.name: JS_AddGCRef
functions.description: Adds a JSGCRef to a GC root list that allows removal in any order (slower than the stack-based variant). Returns a pointer to a JSValue slot for the reference.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
ref must point to a valid, writable JSGCRef whose lifetime continues until explicitly removed with JS_DeleteGCRef.
Entries in this list can be removed in any order (per comment).

functions.name: JS_DeleteGCRef
functions.description: Removes a previously added JSGCRef from the GC root list, undoing JS_AddGCRef for that entry.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
ref must have been previously added with JS_AddGCRef and not yet deleted.

functions.name: JS_NewFloat64
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript number value from a C double.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_NewInt32
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript number value from a 32-bit signed integer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_NewUint32
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript number value from a 32-bit unsigned integer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_NewInt64
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript number value from a 64-bit signed integer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_IsInt
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is a tagged 31-bit integer (implementation-specific integer tag).
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsPtr
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is a tagged pointer value (engine-internal pointer representation).
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsShortFloat
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is a tagged short float (only when built with short float support).
requirements: Available only when compiled with JS_USE_SHORT_FLOAT defined.
v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsBool
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is a boolean.
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsNull
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is the JavaScript null value.
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsUndefined
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is the JavaScript undefined value.
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsUninitialized
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue is an internal uninitialized value (engine special value).
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_IsException
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the JSValue represents an exception indicator.
requirements: v can be any JSValue.

functions.name: JS_NewBool
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript boolean value from a C int (non-zero becomes true, zero becomes false).
requirements: No special requirements; val is treated as boolean.

functions.name: JS_IsNumber
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is a JavaScript Number. Context may be used for additional checks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_IsString
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is a JavaScript String.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_IsError
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is an Error object.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_IsFunction
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the value is a function (C function or JS function).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_GetClassID
functions.description: Returns the internal class ID of an object value. Useful to distinguish engine object classes.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
val should be an object; behavior for non-objects is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: JS_SetOpaque
functions.description: Associates an opaque user pointer with an object value for later retrieval via JS_GetOpaque.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
val should be an object that supports opaque storage (typically user classes).

functions.name: JS_GetOpaque
functions.description: Retrieves the opaque user pointer previously associated to an object via JS_SetOpaque.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
val should be an object on which JS_SetOpaque was previously called.

functions.name: JS_NewContext
functions.description: Creates a new JavaScript execution context using a caller-provided memory region and optional standard library definition.
requirements: mem_start must point to a memory region at least mem_size bytes long and suitably aligned for the engine’s allocations.
The memory region must remain valid for the lifetime of the context.
stdlib_def may be NULL or must point to a valid JSSTDLibraryDef for builtins (per usage pattern).

functions.name: JS_NewContext2
functions.signature: JSContext *JS_NewContext2(void *mem_start, size_t mem_size, const JSSTDLibraryDef *stdlib_def, JS_BOOL prepare_compilation);
functions.description: Creates a new JS context with an additional flag to prepare for compilation to a binary file. Not expected to be used in the embedded version when prepare_compilation is true.
requirements: mem_start must point to a memory region at least mem_size bytes long.
The memory region must remain valid for the lifetime of the context.

functions.name: JS_FreeContext
functions.description: Destroys a JSContext and releases associated resources.
requirements: ctx must have been created by JS_NewContext/JS_NewContext2 and not previously freed.
After this call, ctx must not be used.

functions.name: JS_SetContextOpaque
functions.description: Associates an opaque user pointer with the JSContext for application use.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_SetInterruptHandler
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked to decide whether JS execution should be interrupted. The handler returns non-zero to request interruption.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
interrupt_handler may be NULL to clear the handler.

functions.name: JS_SetRandomSeed
functions.description: Sets the random seed used by the engine.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_GetGlobalObject
functions.description: Returns the global object of the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_Throw
functions.description: Throws a JS exception represented by the given value and returns an exception indicator. Typically used within C code to signal errors to JS.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
obj should be an Error object or value appropriate for throwing.

functions.name: JS_ThrowError
functions.signature: JSValue __js_printf_like(3, 4) JS_ThrowError(JSContext *ctx, JSObjectClassEnum error_num, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Formats and throws a JS Error of the specified class (e.g., TypeError, RangeError) using a printf-style format string and arguments. Returns an exception indicator value.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
error_num must be one of the defined error classes (e.g., JS_CLASS_TYPE_ERROR).
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string, and variadic arguments must match the format (enforced by compiler attribute).

functions.name: JS_ThrowOutOfMemory
functions.description: Throws an out-of-memory exception and returns an exception indicator.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValue this_obj, const char *str);
functions.description: Gets a property by C string name from the given object and returns its value or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
this_obj should be an object value.
str must point to a valid null-terminated UTF-8 property name.

functions.name: JS_GetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: JSValue JS_GetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValue obj, uint32_t idx);
functions.description: Gets an indexed property (array index) from the given object and returns its value or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
obj should be an object value.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyStr
functions.signature: JSValue JS_SetPropertyStr(JSContext *ctx, JSValue this_obj, const char *str, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets a named property on the given object to the specified value. Returns a status value (implementation-specific).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
this_obj should be an object value.
str must point to a valid null-terminated property name.

functions.name: JS_SetPropertyUint32
functions.signature: JSValue JS_SetPropertyUint32(JSContext *ctx, JSValue this_obj, uint32_t idx, JSValue val);
functions.description: Sets an indexed property on the given object to the specified value. Returns a status value (implementation-specific).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
this_obj should be an object value.

functions.name: JS_NewObjectClassUser
functions.description: Creates a new object instance of a user-defined class identified by class_id.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
class_id should correspond to a valid registered user class (inferred from name and enum JS_CLASS_USER).

functions.name: JS_NewObject
functions.description: Creates a new plain JavaScript object.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_NewArray
functions.description: Creates a new JavaScript array with an initial length hint.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
initial_len should be non-negative (inferred from parameter name).

functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionParams
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewCFunctionParams(JSContext *ctx, int func_idx, JSValue params);
functions.description: Creates a C function object backed by an entry in the C function table, with an object parameter used as a closure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
func_idx should refer to a valid entry in the c_function_table (inferred from surrounding types).

functions.name: JS_Parse
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Parse(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Parses JavaScript source (or JSON/RegExp with flags) into an internal representation (bytecode/module). Returns a value representing compiled code or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
input must point to a buffer of at least input_len bytes.
filename should point to a valid string if provided; may be used for diagnostics.
eval_flags should be a combination of JS_EVAL_* flags defined in the header.

functions.name: JS_Run
functions.description: Runs previously parsed/compiled code represented by val and returns the result or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
val should be a value returned by JS_Parse or JS_LoadBytecode.

functions.name: JS_Eval
functions.signature: JSValue JS_Eval(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len, const char *filename, int eval_flags);
functions.description: Parses and executes JavaScript source in one step. Returns the evaluation result or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
input must point to a buffer of at least input_len bytes.
filename should point to a valid string if provided.
eval_flags should be a combination of JS_EVAL_* flags.

functions.name: JS_GC
functions.description: Triggers garbage collection in the engine.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_NewStringLen
functions.signature: JSValue JS_NewStringLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *buf, size_t buf_len);
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript string from a byte buffer with explicit length (need not be null-terminated).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
buf must point to at least buf_len bytes.

functions.name: JS_NewString
functions.description: Creates a JavaScript string from a null-terminated C string.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
buf must point to a null-terminated string.

functions.name: JS_ToCStringLen
functions.signature: const char *JS_ToCStringLen(JSContext *ctx, size_t *plen, JSValue val, JSCStringBuf *buf);
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a C string, storing the length via plen and writing into a small temporary buffer structure provided by the caller. Returns a pointer to a C string or NULL on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
plen must be a valid pointer if non-NULL to receive the length.
buf must point to a writable JSCStringBuf provided by the caller.

functions.name: JS_ToCString
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a C string using a provided temporary buffer. Returns a pointer to a C string or NULL on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
buf must point to a writable JSCStringBuf.

functions.name: JS_ToString
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a JavaScript string value. Returns the string or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_ToInt32
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a 32-bit signed integer. Writes the result to pres and returns 0 on success or non-zero on failure (inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
pres must be a valid pointer to int for the conversion result.

functions.name: JS_ToUint32
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a 32-bit unsigned integer. Writes the result to pres and returns a status code (inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
pres must be a valid pointer to uint32_t.

functions.name: JS_ToInt32Sat
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a 32-bit signed integer with saturation semantics. Writes result to pres and returns a status code (inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
pres must be a valid pointer to int.

functions.name: JS_ToNumber
functions.description: Converts a JS value to a Number (double). Writes result to pres and returns a status code (inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
pres must be a valid pointer to double.

functions.name: JS_GetException
functions.description: Retrieves the current pending exception value from the context (and typically clears it).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_StackCheck
functions.description: Ensures there is enough stack space for len stack slots/bytes (engine-internal unit) before performing an operation. Returns 0 on success or non-zero on failure (inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_PushArg
functions.description: Pushes an argument value onto the call stack in preparation for JS_Call.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
Callers should push arguments in the order expected by the callee before invoking JS_Call (inferred from naming and pairing).

functions.name: JS_Call
functions.description: Invokes a function call prepared on the VM stack. call_flags encodes the argument count in the low bits; for C constructors, FRAME_CF_CTOR may be ORed with argc (per comment). Returns the call result or an exception on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
Before calling, the caller should have pushed the callee/this/arguments as required by the VM ABI and as implied by JS_PushArg (inferred).
call_flags must encode argc appropriately; for constructors, OR with FRAME_CF_CTOR as noted.

functions.name: JS_PrepareBytecode
functions.signature: void JS_PrepareBytecode(JSContext *ctx, JSBytecodeHeader *hdr, const uint8_t **pdata_buf, uint32_t *pdata_len, JSValue eval_code);
functions.description: Host-only: prepares bytecode output from compiled code for writing to a file. Fills header and provides a pointer/length to the data buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
hdr, pdata_buf, and pdata_len must be valid writable pointers.
eval_code should be a value representing compiled code.

functions.name: JS_RelocateBytecode2
functions.signature: int JS_RelocateBytecode2(JSContext *ctx, JSBytecodeHeader *hdr, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t buf_len, uintptr_t new_base_addr, JS_BOOL update_atoms);
functions.description: Host-only: relocates bytecode contained in buf to a new base address, optionally updating atoms. Returns 0 if OK, non-zero on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
hdr must point to a valid JSBytecodeHeader associated with the bytecode.
buf must point to a buffer of at least buf_len bytes containing the bytecode.

functions.name: JS_PrepareBytecode64to32
functions.signature: int JS_PrepareBytecode64to32(JSContext *ctx, JSBytecodeHeader32 *hdr, const uint8_t **pdata_buf, uint32_t *pdata_len, JSValue eval_code);
functions.description: Host-only on 64-bit builds (JSW == 8): produces a 32-bit bytecode image from a 64-bit host for cross-execution. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: Available only when JSW == 8 (64-bit pointers).
ctx must be a valid JSContext.
hdr, pdata_buf, and pdata_len must be valid writable pointers.

functions.name: JS_IsBytecode
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the buffer appears to contain Micro QuickJS bytecode (checks magic/version minimally).
requirements: buf must point to a buffer of at least buf_len bytes.

functions.name: JS_RelocateBytecode
functions.description: Relocates bytecode in-place so that it can be executed later. Returns 0 if OK, non-zero if error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
buf must point to a buffer of at least buf_len bytes containing relocatable bytecode.

functions.name: JS_LoadBytecode
functions.description: Loads precompiled bytecode from buf into the context. Use JS_Run to execute it. Warning from header: the bytecode is not checked, so it should come from a trusted source, and the buffer must remain allocated as long as the JSContext exists.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
buf must remain allocated and unchanged for the entire lifetime of the JSContext (per comment).
Only load trusted bytecode (per comment).

functions.name: JS_SetLogFunc
functions.description: Sets a logging output function used by debug/printing utilities.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
write_func must be a function of signature void(void *opaque, const void *buf, size_t buf_len); may be NULL to disable logging.

functions.name: JS_PrintValue
functions.description: Prints a JavaScript value using the registered log function.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

functions.name: JS_PrintValueF
functions.signature: void JS_PrintValueF(JSContext *ctx, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Prints a JavaScript value with formatting flags for detail and quoting (e.g., JS_DUMP_LONG, JS_DUMP_NOQUOTE, JS_DUMP_RAW).
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
flags should be a combination of JS_DUMP_* flags.

functions.name: JS_DumpValueF
functions.signature: void JS_DumpValueF(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, JSValue val, int flags);
functions.description: Dumps a label and a JavaScript value using the logging function, with control flags.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
str must be a valid C string label.
flags should be a combination of JS_DUMP_* flags.

functions.name: JS_DumpValue
functions.signature: void JS_DumpValue(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, JSValue val);
functions.description: Dumps a label and a JavaScript value using the logging function with default formatting.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.
str must be a valid C string label.

functions.name: JS_DumpMemory
functions.description: Dumps memory/heap statistics, optionally in a long form when is_long is true.
requirements: ctx must be a valid JSContext.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_IsShortFloat
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on build-time flag JS_USE_SHORT_FLOAT; cannot reliably exercise across builds.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_IsUninitialized
unharnessable_functions.reason: Internal engine-only sentinel value with no public constructor; cannot be created via API.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_NewCFunctionParams
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid c_function_table in the context’s stdlib, which this harness does not provide.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_PushArg
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on internal VM call stack ABI and a prepared call frame, which cannot be safely constructed in this fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_Call
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires prior precise VM stack setup (callee/this/args and flags) not exposed by the public API, making safe harnessing infeasible.

unharnessable_functions.name: JS_PrepareBytecode64to32
unharnessable_functions.reason: This function is only available when building with JSW == 8 (64-bit host) and may be absent on the current toolchain.

data_types.description: A raw byte buffer with no required encoding or terminator. May contain any byte values including nulls. Suitable for APIs that accept a pointer and explicit length.
A null-terminated UTF-8/byte string suitable for const char* parameters that expect a property name, label, or message. Must be terminated by a single NUL byte; content otherwise unconstrained.

Text buffer intended to be valid JavaScript program/module source (or related syntaxes controlled by eval/parse flags). May include arbitrary code; parsers treat it as source text using provided length.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for arbitrary bytes meant to be fed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Target stubs mostly create JS strings from these bytes, use them as property names, error messages,
# and as generic byte blobs for JS_IsBytecode. So we focus on producing:
# - Valid UTF-8-ish text (including mixed ASCII, Unicode) to exercise string paths
# - Bytes with embedded NULs to ensure length-based handling
# - Property-like identifiers and dotted paths to hit JS_Get/SetPropertyStr typical cases
# - JavaScript snippets to be potentially useful in other stubs if reused
# - Candidate QuickJS bytecode-like headers to sometimes flip JS_IsBytecode to true
# All within 4096 bytes.

MAX_LEN = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"foo", b"bar", b"baz", b"qux", b"alpha", b"beta", b"gamma", b"delta",
    b"prop", b"name", b"value", b"message", b"length", b"constructor", b"toString",
    b"__proto__", b"prototype", b"Symbol", b"stack", b"code",
]

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "π", "✓", "漢字", "😀", "💾", "🚀", "𝛼", "𝑓", "€", "©", "🧪",
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢", "نص", "тест", "δοκιμή", "テスト", "테스트", "পরীক্ষা",
]

JS_SNIPPETS = [
    b"var x = 1; x;",
    b"({a:1,b:2}).b",
    b"'hello' + ' world'",
    b"function f(a){return a*a;} f(7);",
    b"try{throw new TypeError('msg')}catch(e){e.name}",
    b"let o = {}; o['prop']=42; o.prop;",
    b"[1,2,3].map(x=>x+1).join(',')",
]

IDENT_START = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ$_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + b"0123456789"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    first = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    rest = bytes(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return bytes([first]) + rest


def _random_unicode_bytes(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    s = "".join(rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS) for _ in range(count))
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")


def _with_nuls(rng: random.Random, data: bytes, chance: float = 0.5) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() > chance or not data:
        return data
    # Insert a few NULs at random positions
    b = bytearray(data)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, min(4, max(1, len(b)//16+1)))):
        pos = rng.randrange(0, len(b))
        b[pos] = 0
    return bytes(b)


def _maybe_repeat(rng: random.Random, data: bytes, max_total: int) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        return data
    reps = 1
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        reps = rng.randint(2, min(8, max_total // max(1, len(data))))
    return (data * reps)[:max_total]


def _make_property_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create dotted or bracketed property paths to exercise SetPropertyStr name parsing
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_ident(rng))
        else:
            # include unicode in name
            uni = _random_unicode_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 2))
            # ensure valid identifier-ish by stripping spaces
            uni = uni.replace(b" ", b"")
            parts.append(uni[:rng.randint(1, min(16, max(1, len(uni))))] or b"x")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return b".".join(parts)
    else:
        # bracket style like ["name"]
        return b"[\"" + b"\"][\"".join(parts) + b"\"]"


def _maybe_js_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        return rng.choice(JS_SNIPPETS)
    return b""

def _header_like_quickjs_bytecode(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Try to look like a JS bytecode header for JS_IsBytecode heuristic
    # JSBytecodeHeader: uint16_t magic; uint16_t version; uintptr_t base; JSValue unique; JSValue main
    # Real magic/version are engine-specific; we craft plausible small-endian values.
    magic = rng.choice([0xB0EC, 0xB1EC, 0x4A53])  # fictive candidates
    version = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 0x0100])
    # Use 64-bit layout conservatively; engines typically tolerate pointer-sized fields
    base_addr = rng.getrandbits(64)
    unique = rng.getrandbits(64)
    mainf = rng.getrandbits(64)
    hdr = struct.pack("<HHQQQ", magic, version, base_addr, unique, mainf)
    # Followed by some payload bytes
    payload = bytearray()
    # Insert some atoms-like strings with lengths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        s = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        l = len(s)
        payload += struct.pack("<I", l)
        payload += s
    # Align to 4 bytes
    while len(payload) % 4:
        payload += b"\x00"
    return hdr + bytes(payload)


def _compose_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    chunks = []

    # 1) Identifier/property names
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.append(_make_property_name(rng))
    chunks.append(b"\n")

    # 2) Mixed ASCII words and punctuation
    words = [rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10))]
    sep = rng.choice([b" ", b",", b";", b"|", b"::"])  # variety
    chunks.append(sep.join(words))
    chunks.append(b"\n")

    # 3) Unicode heavy string
    uni_bytes = _random_unicode_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 5))
    chunks.append(uni_bytes)
    chunks.append(b"\n")

    # 4) Optional JavaScript snippet
    js_code = _maybe_js_snippet(rng)
    if js_code:
        chunks.append(js_code)
        chunks.append(b"\n")

    # 5) Include NULs to test length-respecting paths
    nul_block = _with_nuls(rng, b"NUL\x00inside\x00string", chance=1.0)
    chunks.append(nul_block)
    chunks.append(b"\n")

    # 6) Sometimes prepend a header that may trigger JS_IsBytecode true path
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        chunks.insert(0, _header_like_quickjs_bytecode(rng))

    # 7) Optionally repeat some content to grow size and test longer strings
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    data = _maybe_repeat(rng, data, MAX_LEN)

    # 8) Trim or pad slightly with random bytes
    if len(data) < MAX_LEN and rng.random() < 0.3:
        tail = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 64)))
        data += tail
    return data[:MAX_LEN]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = _compose_buffers(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty to be useful for string creation
    if not buf:
        return b"x"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid C strings (null-terminated) tailored to Micro QuickJS fuzz stubs
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for:
# - property names (JS_GetPropertyStr, JS_SetPropertyStr)
# - string creation (JS_NewString)
# - labels for dumps (JS_DumpValueF, JS_DumpValue)
# Requirements: produce null-terminated UTF-8/byte strings. Content can vary to trigger
# different behaviors (identifiers, unicode, empty, long, numeric, special chars, embedded NUL not allowed
# before terminator).

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

# Some interesting property/label strings to exercise different code paths
INTERESTING_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty string
    "a",  # single char
    "_",  # underscore
    "$",  # dollar (valid identifier char in JS)
    "0",  # numeric-looking
    "length",  # common array property
    "prototype",  # common property
    "constructor",
    "toString",
    "valueOf",
    "__proto__",
    "hasOwnProperty",
    "NaN",
    "Infinity",
    "undefined",
    "null",
    "true",
    "false",
    # Unicode and combining marks
    "π",
    "你好",
    "𝒜𝓁𝓅𝒽𝒶",
    "e",  # e with combining acute
    # Escapes/specials that are still valid bytes (just bytes here)
    "prop with space",
    "line\nbreak",
    "tab\tchar",
    "quote\"single'",
    # Long-ish identifier-like
    "veryLongPropertyName_used_for_testing_edge_cases_1234567890",
]

# Ranges of unicode to include for diverse UTF-8
UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplement
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
    (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified Ideographs
    (0x1F600, 0x1F64F), # Emojis
]

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "$_" + "\u00A2"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits


def _rand_unicode_char(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
    cp = rng.randint(block[0], block[1])
    # Skip surrogate range
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0xE000
    try:
        return chr(cp)
    except ValueError:
        return "?"


def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    start = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(max(0, n - 1)))
    return start + rest


def _rand_path_like(rng: random.Random, max_segments: int = 5) -> str:
    segs = []
    count = rng.randint(1, max_segments)
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            segs.append(_rand_identifier(rng, 1, 12))
        else:
            # include dots and dashes
            letters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
            seg_len = rng.randint(1, 12)
            segs.append(''.join(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(seg_len)))
    return '/'.join(segs)


def _rand_utf8_string(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII, unicode, whitespace, punctuation
    parts = []
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:.,[]{}()@#%+")
        elif t < 0.9:
            ch = _rand_unicode_char(rng)
        else:
            ch = rng.choice(["\t", "\n", "\r"])
        parts.append(ch)
    return ''.join(parts)


def _compose_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Predefined interesting values
    for s in INTERESTING_STRINGS:
        pool.append(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # 2) Identifier-like names
    for _ in range(8):
        pool.append(_rand_identifier(rng).encode('utf-8'))

    # 3) Path-like and dotted names
    for _ in range(4):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pool.append(_rand_path_like(rng).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            parts = [_rand_identifier(rng, 1, 8) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))]
            pool.append('.'.join(parts).encode('utf-8'))

    # 4) Random UTF-8 text bursts including unicode
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(_rand_utf8_string(rng, max_len=rng.randint(0, 256)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 5) Numeric-like strings
    for _ in range(5):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pool.append(str(rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            pool.append(("%.8f" % rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 6) Long string near but under cap to exercise JS_NewStringLen/JS_NewString
    long_ascii = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(512, 1500)))
    pool.append(long_ascii.encode('utf-8'))

    # Ensure no embedded NUL; if any, replace with space (FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects C string)
    fixed_pool = []
    for b in pool:
        if b"\x00" in b:
            b = b.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        fixed_pool.append(b)
    return fixed_pool


def _pack_multiple_null_terminated(chunks: List[bytes], max_total: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate multiple C strings separated by NUL terminators so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    # can consume distinct interesting strings from one buffer.
    out = bytearray()
    for b in chunks:
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > max_total:
            break
        out += b
        out.append(0)
    # Guarantee at least one terminator
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    pool = _compose_pool(rng)

    # Select a diverse subset for this buffer
    rng.shuffle(pool)

    # Bias to include: identifier, unicode, empty, dotted, numeric, long
    chosen: List[bytes] = []

    # Always include empty, an identifier, unicode, dotted/path, numeric, and long if present
    # Empty
    empty = next((b for b in pool if len(b) == 0), b"")
    chosen.append(empty)

    # Identifier-like
    ident = next((b for b in pool if b and all(chr(c).isalnum() or chr(c) in "$_" for c in b)), None)
    if ident is None and pool:
        ident = pool[0]
    if ident is not None:
        chosen.append(ident)

    # Unicode (non-ASCII)
    uni = next((b for b in pool if any(c >= 0x80 for c in b)), None)
    if uni is not None:
        chosen.append(uni)

    # Dotted/path-like
    dotted = next((b for b in pool if b"." in b or b"/" in b), None)
    if dotted is not None:
        chosen.append(dotted)

    # Numeric-like
    numeric = next((b for b in pool if b and all(chr(c) in "+-0123456789" for c in b)), None)
    if numeric is not None:
        chosen.append(numeric)

    # Long
    longb = next((b for b in pool if len(b) >= 512), None)
    if longb is not None:
        chosen.append(longb)

    # Add a few random others to diversify calls across different stubs
    for b in pool:
        if len(chosen) >= 20:
            break
        if b not in chosen and rng.random() < 0.3:
            chosen.append(b)

    # Final packing with NUL terminators, size-capped
    buf = _pack_multiple_null_terminated(chosen, min(MAX_TOTAL_SIZE, 4096), rng)
    return buf
